subject: history
title: Civil War and Regicide 1642-49
welcome_lead: From Charles I's personal rule to the scaffold at Whitehall.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on the English Civil War, the New Model Army and the regicide of 1649.
final_note: You have walked from Edgehill to the execution block.

concepts.def: Charles I's eleven-year rule without Parliament, 1629-40, funded by ship money and prerogative income.
Parliament summoned in November 1640 that impeached Strafford and passed reforms before war.
Professional parliamentary army created in 1645 under Fairfax and Cromwell.
Decisive parliamentary victory on 14 June 1645 destroying Charles I's main field army.
Forcible exclusion of moderate MPs by Colonel Pride on 6 December 1648, creating the Rump Parliament.
Trial and execution of Charles I on 30 January 1649 outside the Banqueting House.

walkthroughs.h2: Why did Charles I and Parliament go to war?
walkthroughs.body_html: Religious tensions intensified by Archbishop Laud's reforms, financial disputes over ship money (Hampden's Case 1637) and the Scottish Bishops' Wars (1639-40) forced Charles to recall Parliament. After the 1641 Grand Remonstrance and his failed January 1642 arrest of the Five Members, Charles raised his standard at Nottingham on 22 August 1642, beginning open civil war.

walkthroughs.h2: The New Model Army's military revolution
walkthroughs.body_html: Created by the Self-Denying Ordinance and February 1645 ordinance, the New Model Army of 22,000 men was paid, disciplined and promoted on merit. At Naseby on 14 June 1645 it crushed the royalist army, capturing Charles's correspondence with Catholic Irish. The army became a political actor, presenting the Heads of Proposals in 1647 and ultimately pushing for regicide.

Charles's secret Engagement with the Scots triggered the Second Civil War in 1648. After parliamentary victory at Preston, the army demanded justice. Pride's Purge on 6 December 1648 left a Rump willing to try the king. Charles refused to plead. He was beheaded on 30 January 1649; England was declared a Commonwealth in May, an unprecedented republican experiment.
